lines: Ever catch yourself nodding while your brain’s already elsewhere?
You’re in a stand‑up, eyes on the screen, but your thoughts wander.
That drift means you miss key updates and waste the whole team’s time.
Our minds treat a brief pause as a cue to switch modes, especially with chat‑AI suggestions popping up.
The brain fills the gap with imagined replies, so you think you’re listening when you’re not.
Recognizing that gap—realizing you’re drafting a reply instead of hearing—creates a metacognitive checkpoint.
Imagine you see an AI‑generated agenda suggestion and start typing before the speaker finishes.
By the time they finish, you’ve already missed the next task assignment.
When you notice the urge to type, pause the draft and say “hold on”.
Count silently to three, then refocus on the speaker’s voice.
After the stand‑up, jot a quick note of what you missed and why.
Repeat this pause‑and‑reflect loop for each meeting to train your attention muscle.
Save this reel so you can revisit the tip.
